contracts.commit_point: The in-line time.sleep(delay) inside rate_limit_callback (callbacks.py:73) blocks the model invocation path before the callback returns; the model request can only proceed after the callback returns with the window state reset (callbacks.py:74-79). The actual network dispatch of the LLM request occurs in framework code after the callback returns and is not present in the supplied source.
contracts.declared_mechanism: rate_limit_callback registered as before_model_callback on the root_agent Agent (admission_advisor/agent.py:64). The callback initializes 'timer_start' and 'request_count' in callback_context.state on first invocation (callbacks.py:49-57), increments request_count on subsequent model requests (callbacks.py:59), and when request_count > RPM_QUOTA computes delay = RATE_LIMIT_SECS - elapsed_secs + 1 and calls time.sleep(delay) before resetting 'timer_start' and 'request_count' (callbacks.py:69-75); otherwise it persists the incremented count (callbacks.py:76-77).
contracts.forbidden_condition: More than RPM_QUOTA=10 LLM model requests being issued within a RATE_LIMIT_SECS=60-second window for the agent session — i.e., request_count exceeding RPM_QUOTA relative to the stored 'timer_start' — without the quota delay being applied before the request proceeds (callbacks.py:59-71).

contracts.protection_obligation: Throttle the agent's LLM model invocations to at most RPM_QUOTA=10 requests per RATE_LIMIT_SECS=60-second window by interposing an in-line delay (time.sleep) on any request that would exceed the quota, before the model request is allowed to proceed on the root_agent's model invocation path.

The callback always returns None (callbacks.py:57, 79), so the guard delays rather than rejects or cancels requests; no hard blocking behavior is enforced by this mechanism.
